# Retire the dormant pointer-path vessel conversion and park machinery

## Context

#19533 (operator decision, 2026-10-10) gives a pointer drag one rule for every window of the group. Inside a window it is that window's tab-header proxy; outside every window it is a vessel; leaving a window opens a fresh vessel (docking design record §2.8.6, amended there). `TabSortZone#resolveRemoteDragTransition` now hands a claimed frame straight to the claiming window, so the pointer-path conversion sensor, its park and its re-show are no longer reached. #19533 changed behaviour and kept that code dormant so the release PR stayed reviewable; this ticket deletes it.

## The Problem

Dormant code that still reads as live costs every reader. The conversion events, host handlers and park effects look wired, unit specs keep exercising them, and the size-calibrated park matrix in `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` is skipped rather than gone.

## The Architectural Reality

Unreached since #19533. Each item is verified with a caller census before deleting. The native title-bar drop keeps its own park through `nativeVesselParkHandlers` and must survive.

- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/TabSortZone.mjs`:
  - `getVesselConversionSensor` with `onConvertIn` / `onConvertOut`;
  - the replay scheduling;
  - the `conversionActive` branches in `processDragEnd` / `onDragCancel` (`dockVesselConversionTerminal`, `dockVesselConversionRetired`).
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselConversion.mjs` and its unit spec.
- `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs`: the `dockVesselConversion*` listeners and options.
- `src/manager/DragCoordinator.mjs`: the transition protocol's `retain`, `preview`, `commitEligible` and `replayAfterTransition` branches. The claim resolver never returns them.
- Hosts:
  - `apps/workstation/view/VesselWorkspace.mjs`: `onDockVesselConversion*`, the pointer `vesselParkHandlers`, `resolveVesselConversionSourceRect`, and the pointer branch of `parkTearOutVessel`;
  - `examples/dashboard/crossWindow/DemoBWorkspace.mjs`: the same family.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/NativeVesselTransaction.mjs`:
  - the pointer park effect, including the corner placement `resolveClearPark`;
  - the pointer dispose and the extent restore;
  - the re-show's `DragDrop` addon calls, which only a parked pointer drag could answer.
- `src/dashboard/dock/window/VesselPark.mjs`: the pointer convert-out (`onConversionOut`, `pendingOut`). The native drop never re-shows mid-gesture.
- `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL.spec.mjs`: the skipped size matrix (`runOverlap`, `MATRIX_CELLS`, `positionTargetForPartialOverlap`) and the helpers only it uses.
- The pointer-conversion arms of `DockTabSortZone.spec`, `DockVesselPark.spec`, `DockNativeVesselTransaction.spec`, `DockLayoutAdapter.spec`, `DragCoordinator.spec`, `Workspace.spec` and `DemoBWorkspace.spec`.

## The Fix

Delete the pointer-path conversion and park, and keep every native title-bar seam: `VesselPark` serves that path alone. The docs that describe the pointer park as live move with it: the docking guides and ADR 0029's resolver contract row. Net negative lines; no behaviour change.

The main-thread `DragDrop` addon's park surface (`parkWindowDrag`, park recovery, orphan recovery) loses its last caller here and is deleted by #19541.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No `dockVesselConversion*` event, handler or option remains; `VesselConversion` is gone.
- [ ] The native title-bar drop keeps parking behind its target after release; its unit and e2e arms are green.
- [ ] The HumanPopupOverlap size matrix and its exclusive helpers are deleted; the foreign-popup arms stay green.
- [ ] The unit suite and the Workstation and dashboard e2e folders are green at their `dev` baseline.

## Contract Ledger

Authority: [ADR 0029](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/agentos/decisions/0029-docking-design.md) §2.3 and §2.8.6, as #19533 amended them. Each retired surface is removed outright, with no fallback to the retired path.

| Surface | Shipped behavior / retirement | Refusal / fallback | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TabSortZone#resolveRemoteDragTransition` → `DragCoordinator#onDragMove` | Input `{draggedItem, pointerInTarget}`. Output `null`, `{engage: false}` or `{engage: true, proxyRect}`; the proxy carries a finite positive extent and finite grab offsets. The `retain`, `preview`, `commitEligible` and replay fields are removed. | `null` keeps the generic suspend/resume path. A throw, a Promise, a malformed record or an invalid proxy refuses engagement, and a lost claim leaves the target. | `DockTabSortZone.spec`, `DragCoordinator.spec`; #19542 AC-1/2 |
| `enableVesselConversion` (host option → `LayoutAdapter` → `TabSortZone`) | The name and effective behavior are unchanged: it opts a source into the claim hand-over above, with `getVesselConversionProxyRect()` as the proxy. The dormant sensor it also armed is deleted. | Off: the resolver returns `null`, so the generic path applies. | Head census: `VesselWorkspace`, `DemoBWorkspace`, `LayoutAdapter` and `TabSortZone` are the only references |
| `LayoutAdapter` conversion callbacks/events and the source-rect request | The `dockVesselConversion*` family, the source-rect resolver and the pointer-exit grace (`vesselConversionPointerExitGraceMs`) are removed. Ordinary tear-out and the cross-zone seams are kept. | Removed outright, with no compatibility fallback to pointer parking. | Head caller census; `DockLayoutAdapter.spec`; host suites |
| Pointer-only park and its effects | Retired: the `VesselConversion` class; the pointer park, dispose, corner placement and extent restore; `VesselPark` convert-out; Demo B's park family. | Close-on-entry and fresh tear-out admission own the pointer lifecycle; there is no fallback to the retired park. | #19542 AC-1/3; Workstation and Demo B evidence |
| Native title-bar park/restore/commit | Unchanged. The drop satisfies the main target, or focuses the popup, moves it and refocuses. It restores on refusal or non-commit and disposes the exact generation on commit. Re-show uses the existing exact route and the content-to-frame conversion. | Strict admission and refusal, refocus compensation and the retained retry authority all remain. | `Workspace.spec`, `DockVesselPark.spec`, `DockNativeVesselTransaction.spec`; eight executed native route/title-bar e2e arms (#19542 AC-2) |
| Main-thread addon and the surviving collaborator shape | The addon park deletion (#19541) and the native-class conversion (#19540) stay separate owned leaves. | This change does not expand into either leaf. | #19542 Deltas |

Rows 1 and 3–6 are Emmy's #19542 RA-1 draft (comment 6097785752), adopted after a census at head `55e96a3122`. Row 2 comes from that same census.

## Out of Scope

Any behaviour change; the native title-bar path; the film; the main-thread addon (#19541).

* refactor(dock): retire the main-thread DragDrop park surface nothing calls (#19541)

#19538 removed the last callers of the addon's window-drag park: parkWindowDrag, the addon's resumeWindowDrag, park and orphan recovery and the windowDragPark* state. What stays is the pointer-follow that in-window and tear-out drags use. The App-worker resumeWindowDrag on sort zones and DragCoordinator is a different surface and stays.

* fix(dock): a refused native window move stays handled once the park bookkeeping is gone (#19541)

The deleted park tracking also held the only rejection handler on the live pointer-follow move. Main.windowMoveTo is async and rejects when a native accessor throws, so the bare call left an unhandled rejection. It now catches; the logical drag frame still flows. The spec stub honours the async contract, and a new arm proves the refusal stays handled, with a positive control on its observer."
